text:
Priya (eng-infra): anyone seeing nvme tail latency + sudden iops drops on the us-west-2 GPU fleet since ~06:15 UTC? Alerts from fsync latency and cleaner jobs overlapping with batch scheduling.
Sam (oncall): seeing it too, alerts firing on nvme_iops_sustained and pod restarts in rack-g. graphs: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/abcd/nvme-usw2 (thumbsup)
Priya (eng-infra): quick grep from /var/log/kern.log on one affected host: 
```
Mar 18 06:16:12 host-17 kernel: nvme0: ctrl shutdown due to background trim pause=1
Mar 18 06:16:13 host-17 kernel: nvme0: io_queued=1200 qdepth=64 write_lat=42ms read_lat=90ms
Mar 18 06:16:13 host-17 cleaner[4212]: gc cycle started, batching 2048 objects
Mar 18 06:16:14 host-17 cleaner[4212]: gc pause triggered, waiting for firmware response
```
Priya (eng-infra): wear counters are nudging up on same host family (WAF spike). This looks like background TRIM/GC timing out and causing large queues + write amplification.
Miguel (eng-runtime): we pushed nvme firmware 2.1.4 to a canary set yesterday (10 nodes) — that firmware had a changelog item about "background TRIM scheduling improvements". suspect regression under sustained small-R/W patterns.
Claire (eng-infra): I ran a quick fio: randomrw 4k 70/30 on an affected host, reproduced read-modify spikes and a 3x increase in write amplification vs 2.1.3. Cleaner runs at full batch size (2048) cause the stall.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0318-7 (severity: medium) — assigned to #eng-infra oncall.
Priya (eng-infra): immediate mitigations proposed: disable cleaner scheduled full-cycles for firmware=2.1.4 nodes, throttle batch size to 32, and drain any long-running batch jobs off those hosts. Also mark hosts for firmware rollback.
Sam (oncall): starting rollback playbook for firmware -> 2.1.3 on affected pool (us-west-2-rack-g). Planning a rolling update with cordon+drain. ETA ~45m. I'll post progress.
Miguel (eng-runtime): quick hotfix to cleaner: set NVME_CLEANER_BATCH=32 and NVME_CLEANER_THROTTLE_MS=100 in deploy env for the next rollout. Command to patch: 
```bash
kubectl set env daemonset/ephemeral-cleaner NVME_CLEANER_BATCH=32 -n infra
kubectl set env daemonset/ephemeral-cleaner NVME_CLEANER_THROTTLE_MS=100 -n infra
```
Claire (eng-infra): note: draining GPUs into other regions temporarily increases cost (inter-region transfer, spot re-allocation churn). recommend prioritizing rollback in-us-west-2 before cross-region moves.
infra-automation-bot: nvme-health-check job triggered; writing list of affected hosts to /tmp/nvme-2.1.4-affected-$(date +%s).
Priya (eng-infra): I'll update the runbook with the firmware correlation and add a proactive probe to detect batch-size sensitivity. Also opening a ticket with vendor for 2.1.4 TRIM timing regression.
Sam (oncall): rolling rollback started against 12 nodes in rack-g. currently at 3/12. will pause if we see any regression.
Claire (eng-infra): small note for postmortem: consider adding adaptive cleaner backpressure based on nvme queue depth (iostat r+w await) to avoid hard stalls.
Priya (eng-infra): thanks all — will post a short summary once rollback completes and vendor responds. (cc @infra-sre)
